text:
The evidence can't say whether fire caused the loss. It shows that tree cover was lost in 2021, but it doesn't identify the cause.

What it does show: Hansen mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 (2.23% of the 3,643.5 ha asset). The JRC 2020 forest map agrees on 98% of the affected area, and later years were observed, so the loss is corroborated. Most of the area (68.1 ha) is mapped as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), with 13.2 ha outside mapped forest and no native forest.

Why it can't answer the fire question: Hansen loss records any stand replacement, whether harvest, fire, storm, or clearing. None of the sources here distinguishes among these. Given the planted-pine context, harvesting is plausible, but that is not established.

To test for fire, you'd need burned-area or fire-activity data (e.g., MODIS/VIIRS burned area or active fire detections) for 2021, or local records.
